record.title: Mitochondrial ROS can carry adaptive signals
record.proposition: Complex-III-dependent oxidant signals contribute to hypoxic HIF stabilisation in tested cell systems. Mitochondrial ROS therefore have physiological signalling roles as well as injury-associated roles.
record.process: Codex bounded SEC follow-up v2: targeted primary Results/Methods recovery, exact-proposition precision and replication appraisal; no default factors, dietary inference or human review inferred.

methodology.name: Existing SEC four-factor anchors and integrated caps

rationale.D: Bell 2007 full primary experiments directly perturb complex-III Qo/Rieske signalling and measure ROS, HIF stabilisation and hydroxylation under hypoxia; this tests the existing cell-scoped proposition without relying solely on Guzy abstract data.
rationale.B: Bell Figures 1–8 include respiratory-incompetent cybrids, control shRNA, retained DMOG responses, loading controls, Qo versus Qi inhibitors, MitoQ versus TPMP and catalase controls. These address generalized respiratory failure and nonspecific ROS explanations; probe specificity, adapted cybrids and incomplete allocation/blinding reporting remain residual concerns (B1).
rationale.P: Bell Figures 1, 4, 5 and 8 report three/four independent experiments and mean/SEM for quantitative contrasts; loading/DMOG controls discriminate HIF signalling from wholesale response loss. These are informative for a qualitative contribution in tested cells; effect magnitude and model boundaries remain uncertain, warranting P1 rather than P2.
rationale.R: Guzy (Schumacker group) and Bell (Chandel group) provide separate empirical lines with non-overlapping author lists, but related 143B/cybrid/Rieske methods and contrary rho0-cell results (Srinivas 2001; Vaux 2001) limit generalisation. R1 credits partial confirmation, not universal oxygen-sensing necessity or a literature citation count.

record.capRationale: D2/B1/P1/R1 raw 5; no D1/B0/P0 cap applies; adjusted 5. No unapproved extra downgrade.
limitations: Hypoxia differs from anoxia; pharmacological respiratory inhibition can perturb multiple sites. This is not evidence for indiscriminate ROS reduction or a dietary-to-brain benefit.
Recover Guzy figures/methods and appraise control performance and uncertainty; compare Bell/Guzy model and research dependencies before a complete SEC.

targetedChecks.access: Primary abstract retrieved from Europe PMC/PubMed; no unavailable full-method quantities inferred.
targetedChecks.assessment: Complex-III function and oxidant signalling were required for the tested hypoxic HIF response. Context-dependent cell signalling; not all oxygen-sensing pathways or physiological states require this mechanism.

targetedChecks.role: supporting; pivotal full primary experiment for the same existing proposition
targetedChecks.access: Complete Europe PMC XML: PMC2064363, figures/captions and Methods
targetedChecks.assessment: Bell et al. (2007): Qo/Rieske perturbations, redox/HIF controls and independent repeats establish an informative scoped signalling contribution; not food or clinical efficacy.

targetedChecks.role: contrasting; boundary on universal respiratory-chain/HIF dependence
targetedChecks.access: Primary abstract, PMID11342528; original full Methods not appraised
targetedChecks.assessment: Srinivas et al. (2001) observed hypoxic HIF responses in rho0 cells; retained as credible heterogeneity rather than excluded as an irrelevant negative.

targetedChecks.access: Primary Blood abstract, Vaux et al. (2001)
targetedChecks.assessment: Hypoxic HIF responses persisted in respiratory-chain-defective cells; constrains any universal requirement interpretation.

retrievalLimited.limitation: Guzy original full paper remains access-limited. Bell full primary evidence supplies the load-bearing appraisal for this cell-scoped synthesis; Guzy quantitative effects are not inferred.

sources.contradictoryAssessment: Srinivas 2001 and Vaux 2001 report retained HIF responses in respiratory-chain-defective cells. These constrain universal necessity; the scored proposition explicitly concerns a contribution in the tested cell systems. Bell separates respiration from Qo redox signalling. Model/probe differences remain unresolved boundaries, not a reason to erase the contrary evidence.

evidenceLocations: Bell 2007 primary abstract, PMID17562787 (targeted complementary check)
Bell 2007 PMC2064363: Figures 1–8 and cell/ROS/immunoblot Methods

record.title: Omega-3 exposure need not reduce mitochondrial ROS emission
record.proposition: Twelve weeks of the tested EPA/DHA fish-oil formulation increased muscle mitochondrial membrane EPA/DHA and maximal succinate-supported ROS-emission capacity without increasing the measured oxidative-damage products.
record.process: Codex bounded SEC follow-up v2: targeted primary Results/Methods recovery, exact-proposition precision and replication appraisal; no default factors, dietary inference or human review inferred.

methodology.name: Existing SEC four-factor anchors and integrated caps

rationale.D: Herbst directly measures the specified formulation, mitochondrial fatty acids, emission and selected damage markers before/after 12 weeks.
rationale.B: The pre/post study has no placebo arm; temporal and behavioural confounding and selective endpoint sensitivity remain. The Finding is kept as a description of measured endpoints, not a causal claim of harm or safety.
rationale.P: Re-examination locates oxidative products in Herbst Figure 5B/C: whole-muscle homogenate 4HNE and protein-carbonyl measurements, n=18, mean/SEM and paired testing. Numeric paired changes, covariance/uncertainty and a justified equivalence boundary are not recovered. A nonsignificant change cannot establish no meaningful increase. The exact existing phrase “without increasing” remains ambiguous between a descriptive test result and an absence claim; no P factor is forced.
rationale.R: One independent pre/post cohort supports the exact formulation/time/endpoint combination in the scoped appraisal; two recruitment rounds are not independent research-group replications.

record.capRationale: No complete total: essential unresolved factors remain; unknown is not zero.
limitations: This pre/post study did not isolate EPA from DHA, establish a specific source-control mechanism, show a whole-fish effect or demonstrate that increased ROS emission was harmful.
Appraise damage-marker effect estimates/uncertainty against a justified boundary; retain the descriptive non-increase without interpreting equivalence or safety.
Damage products were measured in muscle homogenates, not isolated mitochondrial membranes. Existing wording should be reviewed before a no-increase interpretation is scored.

targetedChecks.assessment: Mitochondrial membrane composition and ADP sensitivity changed; maximal ROS emission increased while measured 4HNE and protein oxidation did not. No placebo comparison; tested mixture, not independent effects of either constituent or ordinary fish.

retrievalLimited.limitation: Recover paired raw/summary damage-marker data and resolve the claim wording: propose “no statistically detected increase in the measured whole-muscle markers” for scientific review, without changing the canonical Finding in this scoring pass. Do not equate whole-muscle nulls with absence of mitochondrial injury.

sources.contradictoryAssessment: No significant increase in selected damage markers is retained; equivalence and absence of harm are not established.

evidenceLocations: Herbst 2014 PMC3961091: Figure 5A–C (not Figure 6), whole-muscle homogenate assays; mitochondrial membrane lipid composition is a separate measurement.
record.followUp: Recover paired raw/summary damage-marker data and resolve the claim wording: propose “no statistically detected increase in the measured whole-muscle markers” for scientific review, without changing the canonical Finding in this scoring pass. Do not equate whole-muscle nulls with absence of mitochondrial injury.

record.title: Ubiquinol has a local antioxidant role distinct from electron transport
record.proposition: Reduced CoQ10 inhibited induced lipid peroxidation in beef-heart submitochondrial particles even after vitamin E removal, demonstrating a local protective chemistry separate from its electron-carrier role.
record.process: Codex bounded SEC follow-up v2: targeted primary Results/Methods recovery, exact-proposition precision and replication appraisal; no default factors, dietary inference or human review inferred.

methodology.name: Existing SEC four-factor anchors and integrated caps

rationale.D: Forsmark primary indexed Results, Table I and Figures 1–3 descriptions directly compare extraction/reconstitution in beef-heart submitochondrial particles with no HPLC-detectable vitamin E; this is the exact local chemistry claim, not oral CoQ delivery.
rationale.B: Matched extraction/reconstitution, HPLC composition checks and convergent oxygen-consumption/MDA assays address material identity and nonspecific suppression. Residual protein-bound CoQ, extraction-induced changes, missing biological-batch/dispersion reporting and artificial oxidation remain important concerns (B1).
rationale.P: Recovered Results describe loss and return of oxidation inhibition with extraction/re-addition, near-complete MDA suppression in the relevant reduced-CoQ condition, and absent detectable vitamin E. These controlled qualitative contrasts discriminate a protective capacity from its absence. Effect-size dispersion, detection limits and reproducibility across biological preparations remain uncertain (P1, not P2); no confidence intervals are fabricated.
rationale.R: Independent Yamamoto/Komuro/Niki 1990 and Frei/Kim/Ames 1990 primary experiments corroborate ubiquinol-10 antiperoxidative activity in defined liposomes without requiring co-supplied tocopherol. They differ from Forsmark mitochondrial particles and do not independently reproduce its complete extraction protocol. R1 credits partial mechanism confirmation only.

record.capRationale: D2/B1/P1/R1 raw 5; no D1/B0/P0 cap applies; adjusted 5. No unapproved extra downgrade.
limitations: Reconstitution is not dietary delivery. Endogenous CoQ synthesis, oxidised/reduced forms, supplement formulation, tissue uptake and membrane antioxidant activity are distinct relationships. A mitochondrial-disease trial showed only limited effects and did not establish local antioxidant mediation.
Recover and appraise full figure-level quantitative reporting and independent historical particle experiments for the exact vitamin-E-independent proposition.

targetedChecks.access: Primary abstract examined; PMID2065780. No full-method concentrations extracted.
targetedChecks.assessment: Ubiquinol inhibited lipid peroxidation even without vitamin E. Isolated particle chemistry; no oral delivery, tissue dose or human outcome.

targetedChecks.role: contextual; not independent replication of the core mechanism
targetedChecks.access: Primary abstract retrieved from Europe PMC/PubMed; no unavailable full-method quantities inferred.
targetedChecks.assessment: Small effects on exercise aerobic capacity and post-exercise lactate; other clinically relevant variables did not improve. Not proof of mitochondrial membrane protection or ordinary-food efficacy; disease/formulation-specific exposure.

targetedChecks.role: supporting partial replication; independent liposomal chemistry, not mitochondrial-particle protocol
targetedChecks.access: Primary PubMed/J-STAGE abstract; Scite body is only a 683-character proof note and was NOT treated as full Methods/Results
targetedChecks.assessment: Yamamoto et al. (1990): reduced ubiquinol inhibits oxidation in defined phosphatidylcholine liposomes; oxidised ubiquinone lacks this activity. Model difference retained.

targetedChecks.role: supporting partial replication; independent defined-liposome chemistry
targetedChecks.access: Scite linear primary body, first 8000 characters: Introduction/Methods; primary PubMed abstract for results
targetedChecks.assessment: Frei et al. (1990): purified components, controlled radical initiation and HPLC measurements support direct lipid antiperoxidative chemistry; not an independent submitochondrial-particle protocol.

targetedChecks.role: supporting; recovered original indexed Results and Table I
targetedChecks.access: Publisher PDF indexed Results/Methods passages; original complete PDF not downloaded
targetedChecks.assessment: Forsmark et al. (1991): extraction removes detectable CoQ and tocopherol; re-addition restores the relevant respiratory/antiperoxidative contrasts. Residual bound CoQ acknowledged in the primary Results.

retrievalLimited.limitation: Complete original PDF, biological-batch counts and curve-level dispersion not recovered. P1 is based on controlled qualitative discrimination, not a precise efficacy magnitude; no P2 credit.

sources.contradictoryAssessment: Kagan et al. (1990) proposed tocopherol recycling as mediation; Forsmark directly tested removal/re-addition. Independent model-membrane studies support a direct antiperoxidative component. This does not deny tocopherol synergy or prooxidant reactions under other conditions.

evidenceLocations: Forsmark 1991 abstract and primary PDF page 39 methods
Forsmark indexed original Results p40: Table I and Figures 1–3 descriptions
Yamamoto 1990 primary abstract and Frei 1990 primary Methods/abstract

record.title: Sulforaphane protected mitochondria in defined cell experiments
record.proposition: Sulforaphane pretreatment protected mitochondrial lipids, proteins and enzyme activities in oxidant-challenged SH-SY5Y cells through an Nrf2-dependent mechanism; separate vascular-cell experiments measured induction of mitochondrial defences.
record.process: Codex bounded SEC follow-up v2: targeted primary Results/Methods recovery, exact-proposition precision and replication appraisal; no default factors, dietary inference or human review inferred.

methodology.name: Existing SEC four-factor anchors and integrated caps

rationale.D: Oliveira measures mitochondrial lipid/protein injury and Nrf2 dependence after the stated pretreatment/challenge; Zhu measures the separately described defence induction.
rationale.B: Publisher preview and Scite supply only the abstract for the pivotal Oliveira study. It reports Nrf2 silencing, but non-targeting/knockdown controls, assay validation, biological repeat independence and reporting protections remain unverified. Public figure recovery returned HTML, not a usable figure; no B1/B0 is assigned by default.
rationale.P: No primary figure-level replicate counts, dispersion or dose/knockdown contrasts were recovered. The public abstract and other cell-model studies cannot supply those quantities for the exact SH-SY5Y/H2O2/Nrf2 proposition. Precision remains unresolved rather than P0.
rationale.R: One verified experimental line tests the exact SH-SY5Y injury/Nrf2 proposition. Zhu vascular-cell defence induction differs in model and endpoint and is not exact replication.

record.capRationale: No complete total: essential unresolved factors remain; unknown is not zero.
limitations: This supports preclinical mechanism engagement. Human broccoli-sprout pharmacokinetics establish absorption mainly as conjugated metabolites, not equivalence to sustained free sulforaphane in culture or demonstrated mitochondrial protection from a food.
Recover Oliveira full results, replicate structure, knockdown controls and uncertainty. Keep food absorption evidence separate from protective efficacy.

targetedChecks.access: Primary abstract retrieved from Europe PMC/PubMed; no unavailable full-method quantities inferred.
targetedChecks.assessment: Mitochondrial membrane lipid peroxidation, protein carbonylation/nitration and enzyme inhibition were attenuated; Nrf2 silencing abolished protection. Cell line, imposed oxidant stress and free-compound exposure; not broccoli or human neuronal target engagement.

targetedChecks.access: Primary abstract retrieved from Europe PMC/PubMed; no unavailable full-method quantities inferred.
targetedChecks.assessment: Sulforaphane induced cellular and mitochondrial antioxidant defences and increased resistance to imposed oxidative/electrophilic stress. Mitochondrial defence induction is not the same endpoint as direct mitochondrial membrane injury; not an independent neuronal replication.

retrievalLimited.limitation: Publisher subscription preview and Scite abstract fallback only; usable complete Results/Methods not recovered.

sources.contradictoryAssessment: No exact-proposition contradiction was established in this bounded appraisal. Nonmatching endpoints and tissue/exposure limits remain explicit; this is not an exhaustive absence-of-contradiction claim.

evidenceLocations: Publisher preview and Scite source=abstract/contentDenied=true; figure download returned HTML, not scientific data.
record.followUp: Obtain an authorised full text or author manuscript (Methods, mitochondrial injury figures and Nrf2-silencing controls). Establish biological replicates and uncertainty. No food-effect or human translation conclusion follows from resolving these cellular factors.
